slides.heading: Defining Functions
slides.body: Defining Functions is part of Functions and Modularity. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Defining Functions
slides.body: Defining a function uses the def keyword, a function name, parentheses, a colon, and an indented body.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Defining a function is like writing a procedure in a manual before anyone follows it.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: A good function should do one clear task and have a name that explains that task.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Define a function named show_line that prints -----.
slides.hint: Do not forget the colon after the parentheses.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Define and call a function named display that prints Ready.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
